summary: Round 2 of 2, test review. Both round-1 findings verified. F1 (MAJOR, rename-blindness in check-test-integrity and check-tdd) is accurately recorded as M0.53 and recording rather than fixing was the correct call -- verified line by line against scripts/test_integrity.py:74-88 and scripts/tdd_scan.py:38-47, and re-proved empirically. F2 (MINOR, the cost test commits once) is confirmed genuinely pre-existing and correctly left alone; I now measure it as stronger than round 1 stated and carry it forward as a minor recommending a backlog row. The pure-move property holds byte-for-byte, no assertion anywhere was weakened, and the claimed suite numbers verify exactly.
verified: Pure move, byte-for-byte: diff of HEAD:ingest/.../CommitLog.java against :sequencer/.../CommitLog.java yields exactly one hunk, the package line. Identical for CommitLogTest.java. No assertion, comment or helper differs.

M0.53 accuracy: test_integrity.py:74-76 builds paths from `git diff --cached --name-only`, which for this staged rename emits ONLY the two destination paths (confirmed by running it); line 86 `before = git('show','HEAD:'+p)` returns None because HEAD:sequencer/.../CommitLogTest.java is absent (confirmed); line 88 takes `continue  # new test file: nothing to weaken`. The source path is absent from `paths` entirely, so the removal side is never examined. tdd_scan.py:38-47 has the identical construction (`before = git('show', before_ref + p) or ''  # absent => new file`), so both scanners go blind on the same input, as the row claims. `git diff --cached --name-status -M` does recover the source path, so the proposed fix is the right mechanism. Every specific claim in the row checks out.

M0.53 placement: unique ID (no duplicate backlog IDs anywhere), inserted at backlog.md:31 directly after M0.52 and adjacent to M0.17 -- the two other scanner blind spots -- and genuinely distinct from both (composed annotations; source-set task mapping; this one is rename detection in path enumeration).

Recording rather than fixing was right: the fix touches two scanners and would need its own red-recorded harness tests, breaking one-task-one-commit and destroying the exact pure-move property M4.2 exists to demonstrate. Because the gate is blind here, this commit's test integrity rests on manual byte comparison -- which I performed, above, and which the M4.2 row itself records as its proof.

F2 pre-existing: proved two ways. The staged CommitLogTest is byte-identical to HEAD's except the package line, so no weakness could have been introduced. And I reproduced the mutation at HEAD in an isolated git worktree (never the real tree): deleting the success-path `apply(delta)` at CommitLog.java:134 leaves ALL 93 ingest tests green, 0 failures, 0 errors, including all 9 CommitLogTest tests.
Round-1 minor fixes changed no behaviour: for all six touched non-moved files, every staged +/- line is an `import` or a javadoc `*` line. Zero assertion, arrange or act lines changed.

Import ordering fixed: SearchableIT, ShardFanOutIT and EndToEndTest now sort cleanly. DefaultIngestTest and DefaultIngest are still unsorted, but both were already unsorted at HEAD for unrelated imports (Capabilities/CountingBinStore, TimeUnit); the newly added `binjava.sequencer.CommitLog` sits in its correct slot in all six files.

No dangling reference anywhere: whole-tree grep for `binjava.ingest.CommitLog` finds only backlog prose describing the old test FQN as history; grep for the old path finds nothing; the only javadoc reference is IntervalPutRateTest.java:35, now qualified to `{@link binjava.sequencer.CommitLog}`, and ingest has `api(project(":sequencer"))` so it resolves.
clusterTest compiles: `./gradlew :plugin:compileClusterTestJava` exits 0. `./gradlew test` does not cover that source set, so the two edited IT files were verified separately.

Suite numbers verify exactly: `./gradlew test` exits 0; aggregating every module's JUnit XML gives TOTAL=432, failures=0, errors=0, with ingest=84 and sequencer=26. Consistent with the measured pre-move ingest=93 (93-9=84, 17+9=26).

Working tree clean: `git diff` is empty and `git status --porcelain` shows only staged entries. The transient `apply(delta)` mutation the round-1 production reviewer observed is gone; my own mutation ran in a throwaway worktree that has been removed and pruned.
Backlog row honesty: every factual claim in the M4.2 row that I could check -- pure move, 432/84/26, the seven references, the three reorderings, M0.53 -- is true as written.

findings.title: Carry-over from round 1: the one-request cost invariant is unconstrained beyond the first commit, and this deserves a backlog row rather than only a commit-body line
findings.failure_scenario: `committingCostsExactlyOneRequestWhenUncontended` performs exactly ONE `log.commit(...)` and then asserts `puts()==1` and `total()==1`. Surviving mutation, measured not argued: delete `apply(delta)` from the SUCCESS branch of CommitLog.commit (line 134), leaving the lost-race `apply(readDelta(...))` at line 140 intact. `nextSequence` then never advances on success, so commit #2 issues a doomed putIfAbsent on the already-taken slot 0, a GET to read the winner, and a second putIfAbsent -- three requests where one is correct, with cumulative counts going 1,4,7 instead of 1,2,3. Behaviour is unchanged (line 140 recovers the same offset state), so this is a PURE request-rate regression, which is precisely the class of defect non-negotiable 6 and cost.md exist to prevent. I ran this mutation at HEAD in an isolated worktree: 93 of 93 ingest tests pass, 0 failures, 0 errors -- it survives not just the cost test but the entire module. A second commit plus `assertThat(store.counts().total()).isEqualTo(2)` kills it.
findings.recommendation: Leave the test alone in THIS commit -- correct as staged. It is pre-existing (the staged file is byte-identical to HEAD modulo the package line) and adding an assertion would destroy the pure-move property the task exists to demonstrate. But the parent asked directly whether a commit-body line suffices, and my answer is no: a commit-body line is not a work item and nothing will ever action it, whereas backlog.md is the authoritative task list. M1.10b is the exact precedent -- a CommitLog defect found by mutation, filed as a row. Round 1 characterised this as 'the cost test commits once'; the measurement shows it is broader than that, and the row should carry the measured evidence (survives 93/93) rather than the weaker framing. Does not block: minor, pre-existing, and round 2 is not the place to grow the diff.
